reference_review.review_notes: Current InterPro descriptions and GO mappings were inspected for IPR000537, IPR006369 and IPR016315. The inherited finding is broad shorthand; these mappings have distinct scopes, and the specific inner-membrane refinement also uses independent reaction/location evidence.

Current PTHR43448 topology and MSA place the exact human sequence below both recorded ancestral nodes. Current complete donor records are indexed; historical narrow-term IBD placement was not replayed. Target self-with/from is legitimate descendant grounding.
Current HPA XML authenticates COX10 and reports supported ICC/IF mitochondrial localization. The summary was read; images were not independently interpreted.

Current literal transfer records and official mouse/Ensembl identity were inspected. The matrix donor resolves specifically to PMID:16103131; its scope is qualified in the annotation review. The inherited general finding does not describe every current transferred term.

Complete current ARBA00027066, ARBA00087087 and ARBA00086146 rules match the target in branches 1/20, 0 and 3 respectively (zero-based). Their actual outputs and conditions are preserved, rather than treating the inherited general finding as a literal list of current rules.

The complete current combined records retain their separate InterPro, reaction, EC and donor contributions. The inner-membrane specificity is an authored refinement of the broader current location term.

Identifier and complete abstract verified; actual original author-uploaded Methods, Results, Table 2 and Discussion were read. HPLC rescue brings heme A toward control (about 107% and 81% in the two transduced patient lines), while respiratory immunoblots do not establish COX10 complex membership. External original text supplements the unchanged abstract-only cache.

Identifier/abstract and actual original Methods, Results, Discussion and captions were read in external indexed original text. Patient subassembly patterns support a cofactor-dependent assembly context. The inherited finding uses stronger establishment language than the paper: the order of heme incorporation is an inferred model, not a direct COX10 insertase assay. Cache unchanged; no figure-pixel claim.

The genuine full article Methods/Results and original HTML/XML were read, including its multi-pool inventory construction and explicit COX10 disease-gene mention. Direct supplementary XLSX access returned an HTML challenge; a bounded archive request did not finish. The exact COX10 table row/pool was not verified. The inherited finding must not be read as an independently verified inner-membrane assay from this source.

Identifier and complete cached abstract verified. Actual original author-deposited article Methods, complementation Results, Discussion and captions were recovered as indexed text; no figure pixels were inspected. The protected cache remains abstract-only. Human yeast complementation supports heme farnesylation, not free GGPP synthesis or a purified human assay.
Current hasEvent 189451→2995330 and catalyst/entity/reference chain to Q12887 were verified. The broad event summary describes multiple heme steps; COX10 contributes the specific heme O reaction.

Current 2995330→catalystActivity2995336→physicalEntity2995338→referenceEntity52616 identifies Q12887. Catalyst MF8495 and entity compartment5743 are explicit; event-level matrix context does not locate the enzyme in matrix.

Historical machine-generated report and findings retained. Its independently corroborated reaction/localization points inform synthesis, but every mechanistic, interactome and variant-count detail in the inherited report has not been individually verified. It is a secondary research aid, not a primary experimental source. Its reaction and inner-membrane synthesis is cited as secondary core context, independently corroborated by the primary and curated sources cited alongside it; no independent experiment is attributed to this report.

Genuine full normal source: mouse skeletal-muscle conditional Cox10 deletion, respiratory subunit assays and phenotype. Complete unique Methods/Results/Discussion text was read; figure pixels and omitted captions were not. Its explicit failed Cox10-specific antibody experiments limit a direct matrix-location interpretation.

Complete genuine abstract explicitly describes mouse COX10 knockout and transduction experiments affecting respiratory-complex assembly. It corroborates conserved pathway context; full Methods/Results were not recovered and no new assay details are inferred.

Complete genuine abstract reports direct E. coli CyoE membrane-dependent heme O synthesis from exogenous protoheme and farnesyl diphosphate. This is bacterial experimental grounding for the current donor, not direct human enzymology; full Methods/Results unavailable.

definitions.name: geranylgeranyl diphosphate synthase activity

definition.text: Catalysis of the reaction: (2E,6E)-farnesyl diphosphate + isopentenyl diphosphate = (2E,6E,10E)-geranylgeranyl diphosphate + diphosphate.

definitions.comment: The catalyzed reaction forms (free) geranylgeranyl diphosphate. There is no relationship between this activity and protein farnesyltransferase activity, GO:0004660, where the catalyzed reaction transfers a farnesyl group from farnesyl diphosphate to a target protein.

definition.text: Catalysis of the transfer of a prenyl group from one compound (donor) to another (acceptor).
The selective, non-covalent, often stoichiometric, interaction of a molecule with one or more specific sites on another molecule.

definitions.name: mitochondrion

definition.text: A semiautonomous, self replicating organelle that occurs in varying numbers, shapes, and sizes in the cytoplasm of virtually all eukaryotic cells. It is notably the site of tissue respiration.

definitions.comment: Some anaerobic or microaerophilic organisms (e.g. Entamoeba histolytica, Giardia intestinalis and several Microsporidia species) do not have mitochondria, and contain mitochondrion-related organelles (MROs) instead, called mitosomes or hydrogenosomes, very likely derived from mitochondria. To annotate gene products located in these mitochondrial relics in species such as Entamoeba histolytica, Giardia intestinalis or others, please use GO:0032047 'mitosome' or GO:0042566 'hydrogenosome'. (See PMID:24316280 for a list of species currently known to contain mitochondrion-related organelles.)

definition.text: The inner, i.e. lumen-facing, lipid bilayer of the mitochondrial envelope. It is highly folded to form cristae.

The gel-like material, with considerable fine structure, that lies in the matrix space, or lumen, of a mitochondrion. It contains the enzymes of the tricarboxylic acid cycle and, in some organisms, the enzymes concerned with fatty acid oxidation.
The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the formation of heme, any compound of iron complexed in a porphyrin (tetrapyrrole) ring, from less complex precursors.
The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the formation of heme A, a derivative of heme found in cytochrome aa3.
Catalysis of the reaction: protoheme IX + (2E,6E)-farnesyl diphosphate + H2O = heme O + diphosphate.

The aggregation, arrangement and bonding together of a set of components to form respiratory chain complex IV (also known as cytochrome c oxidase), the terminal member of the respiratory chain of the mitochondrion and some aerobic bacteria. Cytochrome c oxidases are multi-subunit enzymes containing from 13 subunits in the mammalian mitochondrial form to 3-4 subunits in the bacterial forms.
A lipid bilayer along with all the proteins and protein complexes embedded in it and attached to it.

definitions.name: transferase activity, transferring alkyl or aryl (other than methyl) groups

definition.text: Catalysis of the transfer of an alkyl or aryl (but not methyl) group from one compound (donor) to another (acceptor).

synonyms.name: transferase activity, transferring alkyl or aryl groups, other than methyl groups

definition.text: The aggregation, arrangement and bonding together of a cytochrome complex. A cytochrome complex is a protein complex in which at least one of the proteins is a cytochrome, i.e. a heme-containing protein involved in catalysis of redox reactions.
Either of the lipid bilayers that surround the mitochondrion and form the mitochondrial envelope.

definitions.name: protein-containing complex

definition.text: A stable assembly of two or more macromolecules, i.e. proteins, nucleic acids, carbohydrates or lipids, in which at least one component is a protein and the constituent parts function together.

definitions.comment: A protein complex in this context is meant as a stable set of interacting proteins which can be co-purified by an acceptable method, and where the complex has been shown to exist as an isolated, functional unit in vivo. Acceptable experimental methods include stringent protein purification followed by detection of protein interaction. The following methods should be considered non-acceptable: simple immunoprecipitation, pull-down experiments from cell extracts without further purification, colocalization and 2-hybrid screening. Interactions that should not be captured as protein complexes include: 1) enzyme/substrate, receptor/ligand or any similar transient interactions, unless these are a critical part of the complex assembly or are required e.g. for the receptor to be functional; 2) proteins associated in a pull-down/co-immunoprecipitation assay with no functional link or any evidence that this is a defined biological entity rather than a loose-affinity complex; 3) any complex where the only evidence is based on genetic interaction data; 4) partial complexes, where some subunits (e.g. transmembrane ones) cannot be expressed as recombinant proteins and are excluded from experiments (in this case, independent evidence is necessary to find out the composition of the full complex, if known). Interactions that may be captured as protein complexes include: 1) enzyme/substrate or receptor/ligand if the complex can only assemble and become functional in the presence of both classes of subunits; 2) complexes where one of the members has not been shown to be physically linked to the other(s), but is a homologue of, and has the same functionality as, a protein that has been experimentally demonstrated to form a complex with the other member(s); 3) complexes whose existence is accepted based on localization and pharmacological studies, but for which experimental evidence is not yet available for the complex as a whole.

definition.text: A protein complex in which at least one of the proteins is a cytochrome, i.e. a heme-containing protein involved in catalysis of redox reactions.

summation.text: Heme A and less frequently heme O function as prosthetic groups of heme-copper respiratory oxidases(Rivett et al. 2021). Mitochondrial protoheme IX farnesyltransferase (COX10) mediates the transformation of protoheme IX (heme) and farnesyl diphosphate (FAPP) to heme O (Glerum & Tzagoloff 1994). COX10 is highly expressed in muscle, heart and brain (Murakami et al. 1997).

summation.displayName: Although heme is synthesised in virtually all tissues, the p...
summation.text:
Although heme is synthesised in virtually all tissues, the principal sites of synthesis are erythroid cells (~85%) and hepatocytes (most of the remainder). Eight enzymes are involved in heme biosynthesis, four each in the mitochondria and the cytosol (Layer et al. 2010). The process starts in the mitochondria with the condensation of succinyl CoA (from the TCA cycle) and glycine to form 5-aminolevulinate (ALA). The next four steps take place in the cytosol. Two molecules of ALA are condensed to form the monopyrrole porphobilinogen (PBG). The next two steps convert four molecules of PBG into the cyclic tetrapyrrole uroporphyringen III, which is then decarboxylated into coproporphyrinogen III. The last three steps occur in the mitochondria and involve modifications to the tetrapyrrole side chains and finally, insertion of iron. In addition to these synthetic steps, a spontaneous cytosolic reaction allows the formation of uroporphyringen I which is then enzymatically decarboxylated to coproporphyrinogen I, which cannot be metabolized further in humans. Also, lead can inactivate ALAD, the enzyme that catalyzes PBG synthesis, and ferrochelatase, the enzyme that catalyzes heme synthesis (Ponka et al. 1999, Aijoka et al. 2006).

The porphyrias are disorders that arise from defects in the enzymes of heme biosynthesis. Defective pathway enzymes after ALA synthase result in accumulated substrates which can cause either skin problems, neurological complications, or both due to their toxicity in higher concentrations. They are broadly classified as hepatic porphyrias or erythropoietic porphyrias, based on the site of the overproduction of the substrate. Each defect is described together with the reaction it affects (Peoc'h et al. 2016).
